consistency.detail: 25 drugs listed, N = 25 in the regression tables.
MW matches PubChem for 23/25 drugs; fluvoxamine is the maleate salt and desvenlafaxine is printed 263.381 (PubChem 263.37).
CO matches current PubChem for drugs 10-25 only; drugs 1-9 differ (e.g. fluoxetine 296 vs 308, escitalopram 401 vs 466), so the column mixes sources or PubChem versions.

PubChem experimental melting points (PUG-View 'Melting Point', checked 2026-10-03): fluoxetine 179 matches '179 - 182 °C', sertraline 246 matches '245-246'; venlafaxine 215 does not match the base (74-76 °C) and fits a salt form. MP looks measured, partly for salts.
MV is printed 27.3, an order of magnitude below every other drug (likely a dropped digit); kept as printed.
Citalopram and escitalopram have the same hydrogen-suppressed graph but different index values in Table 4 (e.g. NM1 285 vs 280), so at least one row is miscomputed.
Rows 2 and 11 of Table 14 print a different index (ND5 / ND1) from the matching equations in Tables 8 and 10. For MW the LOOCV Q2 (0.7735) exceeds the in-sample R2 (0.609).

Table 11 lists MW as best fitted by a logarithmic ND1 model (R2 0.774), but Table 10 has no MW model (0.774 is the MR logarithmic model); the 'improvement over linear' percentages do not follow from the R2 values (e.g. MR 0.867 -> 0.878 printed as 151.6% higher).
The abstract calls all eight properties 'measured'.

resolution_issues: Fluvoxamine: MW 434.4 and HAC 30 are those of fluvoxamine maleate (PubChem base: 318.33, 22 heavy atoms). The name resolves to the base (CID 5324346); the MW/HAC/CO values of this row describe the salt.
Citalopram and escitalopram share the InChIKey connectivity block (racemate vs S-enantiomer); they must be kept in the same CV fold.

reasons: drug names, all 8 property columns and all 9 index columns are printed; the index definitions are standard neighborhood-degree formulas
linear, quadratic and logarithmic OLS with one index and LOOCV need no free choices

caveats: index symbols in the JATS XML are images (taken from the publisher HTML); several internal inconsistencies (Table 11 vs Tables 5-10, Table 14 symbols, Q2 > R2 for MW) mean some printed numbers cannot all be matched at once
